record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: For every binary pattern p and alphabet size k, classify p with respect to minimum hole sparsity and non-trivial minimum hole sparsity in partial words. Here a partial word is lambda-sparse when every factor of length lambda contains at least one hole; minimum hole sparsity is the smallest positive lambda for which there exists an infinite lambda-sparse partial word over k letters that avoids all occurrences of p, while the non-trivial version only requires avoiding non-trivial occurrences. Determine this lambda for each p and k, or determine that it is infinite when no such partial word exists.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an alphabet be a finite set of letters and let ⋄ denote a special symbol called a hole. A partial word over an alphabet Σ is a (finite or infinite) sequence with entries in Σ ∪ {⋄}; positions containing ⋄ are called holes and are considered compatible with every letter of Σ. A factor of a partial word is any contiguous block of its entries. For a positive integer λ, a partial word is said to be λ-sparse if every factor of length λ contains at least one hole.

A pattern is a nonempty word p over a pattern alphabet of variables. An occurrence of p in a partial word w is a morphism h sending each variable to a nonempty partial word such that the image h(p) is compatible with some factor of w (i.e., matches it in every non-hole position); the occurrence is called trivial if h sends some variable to a partial word consisting of a single hole, and non-trivial otherwise. The partial word w avoids p if no occurrence of p appears in w; it avoids p non-trivially if no non-trivial occurrence appears.

For a binary pattern p (a pattern over an alphabet of two variables) and an integer k ≥ 1, define
- ms(p,k) = the smallest positive integer λ such that there exists an infinite λ-sparse partial word over a k-letter alphabet that avoids p, and ms(p,k) = ∞ if no such infinite λ-sparse partial word exists for any λ;
- ms*(p,k) = the analogous quantity where avoidance is required only non-trivially.

Problem: For every binary pattern p and every alphabet size k ≥ 1, determine the values of ms(p,k) and ms*(p,k) (including determining when they are infinite).
artifact.status_search_result: The minimum hole sparsity classification has been completed for unary patterns in partial words, but the corresponding classification for binary patterns and arbitrary alphabet size k appears to remain an open problem in the literature on avoidable patterns in partial words. No source was found announcing a complete solution for the binary case.

status_evidence.title: Unary Pattern Avoidance in Partial Words Dense with Holes
status_evidence.snippet: Minimum hole sparsity values have been determined for all unary patterns in the context of trivial and non-trivial avoidability.
status_evidence.claim: The unary case is solved, indicating the binary case (with arbitrary k) remains the natural open question.

status_evidence.title: Avoidable binary patterns in partial words
status_evidence.snippet: Work on avoidable binary patterns in partial words; avoidability index considerations.
status_evidence.claim: Binary pattern avoidance in partial words is an active topic with classification questions still investigated.
